title: Whistleblower protection - the corporate governance gaps that remain
p1:
A company can have a whistleblower policy and still fail to protect the truth.

The biggest governance risks often begin when employees notice problems but stay silent.
p2:
Many assume whistleblower protection means having a confidential email address or reporting channel. The real challenge is what happens after a complaint is made.

A system fails when employees fear retaliation, complaints are ignored, or investigations lack independence.
p3:
Strong corporate governance is not just about creating rules; it is about building trust that speaking up will not damage a person's career.

One lesser-known gap is that even anonymous systems can lose credibility if employees believe leadership can identify and target the person who raised concerns.

The practical lesson: a whistleblower framework must protect the process, not just collect complaints.
